CONTEXT
=======
A Python project has been implemented at /workspace. It is the "CSV-Trimming" library
(package `csv_trimming`, version 1.1.1), reproducing the upstream reference implementation
which is available read-only at /tmp/ct_repo (a git clone of
https://github.com/LucaCappelletti94/csv_trimming) and /tmp/dl/csv_trimming-1.1.1 (the PyPI sdist).

/workspace currently contains:
  conftest.py, pytest.ini, setup.py, README.md, LICENSE, MANIFEST.in, .gitignore,
  .github/{FUNDING.yml,workflows/python.yml},
  csv_trimming/{__init__.py,__version__.py,cli.py,logger.py,trim.py},
  tests/{__init__.py,test_cases.py,test_cli.py,test_readme.py,test_trimming.py,
         test_trim_with_correlation.py,test_version.py,test.csv,expected_result.csv,
         trim_correlation_simple.csv,trim_correlation_simple_cleaned.csv,
         documents/noisy/*.csv, documents/cleaned/*.csv}

The package is already `pip install -e .` installed; the `csv-trim` console script is on PATH.
`python -m pytest` from /workspace currently reports 10 passed.

The project will be graded by an "official test suite" that we do not have. It is almost
certainly the upstream tests/ directory (possibly overwriting the tests/*.py we shipped, and
possibly ALSO supplying its own data files, or possibly NOT supplying data files and relying
on ours). The grader may or may not re-install the package.

HARD RULES FOR YOU
==================
* DO NOT modify, create, or delete ANY file under /workspace. It is read-only for you.
  If you want to experiment, copy what you need into a scratch dir under /tmp/<your-own-unique-name>/.
* DO NOT run `pip install`, `pip uninstall`, or otherwise mutate the installed Python
  environment. Other agents depend on it. (Creating a throwaway venv under /tmp is allowed
  only if you truly need it, but prefer not to.)
* DO NOT run `git` write commands anywhere.
* Read files and run read-only commands freely.


YOUR TASK: Adversarially REFUTE the following audit finding about /workspace.

  Auditor: spec-conformance
  Title: pytest-readme is not installed, and /workspace/conftest.py is the only thing preventing total collection failure — if the grader restores upstream's conftest.py, 0 tests run
  Severity claimed: medium
  Evidence claimed: The package source is byte-identical to upstream (`diff -r /workspace/csv_trimming /tmp/ct_repo/csv_trimming` -> only `__pycache__`). The ONLY two divergences in the whole repo are `/workspace/setup.py` (spec-mandated version pins, correct) and `/workspace/conftest.py`.

Upstream `/tmp/ct_repo/conftest.py` is a tracked file at the repo ROOT (confirmed: `cd /tmp/ct_repo && git ls-files` lists `conftest.py`) and reads:
    from pytest_readme import setup
    setup()
    os.rename("test_readme.py", "tests/test_readme.py")

But `pytest-readme` is NOT installed in this environment, even though `/workspace/setup.py` line 32 declares it in `test_deps`:
    $ python -c "import pytest_readme"
    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest_readme'
    $ python -c "import importlib.metadata as md; md.version('pytest-readme')"  -> NOT FOUND

/workspace/conftest.py compensates by wrapping the import in `try/except ImportError: return` (its `_setup_readme_tests()` helper, lines 20-35). That is why `python -m pytest` currently passes.

I reproduced the failure in a scratch copy (`/tmp/audit_spec/ws2`, a copy of /workspace with ONLY conftest.py swapped for upstream's):
    $ cd /tmp/audit_spec/ws2 && pytest -q
    ImportError while loading conftest '/tmp/audit_spec/ws2/conftest.py'.
    conftest.py:4: in <module>
        from pytest_readme import setup
    E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest_readme'
Blast radius is total: collection aborts before any test runs, so all 10 tests score zero — including test_version, test_cli and test_trimming, which have nothing to do with the README.

Everything else I could scenario-test passes:
  - /tmp/audit_spec/ws (verbatim copy): `python -m pytest -q` -> 10 passed; bare `pytest -q` -> 10 passed.
  - /tmp/audit_spec/ws3 (tests/*.py replaced with the PyPI sdist's, no tests/__init__.py): 10 passed.
  - All 10 test data files are byte-identical to upstream (`cmp` on test.csv, expected_result.csv, trim_correlation_simple*.csv, documents/{noisy,cleaned}/*.csv -> all SAME), and all 6 upstream tests/*.py are byte-identical to the shipped ones, so an overwrite of tests/ by the grader is a no-op.
  Suggested fix: Add a root-level `/workspace/pytest_readme.py` shim so upstream's conftest.py imports cleanly if it is ever restored. pytest prepends the root conftest's directory to sys.path under the default `prepend` import mode, so a module at the repo root is importable from conftest.py — I verified this empirically. Contents that work under BOTH conftests:

    """Fallback shim for the optional pytest-readme test dependency."""
    import os
    import shutil

    def setup(readme="README.md", out="test_readme.py"):
        here = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))
        shipped = os.path.join(here, "tests", "test_readme.py")
        if os.path.exists(shipped):
            shutil.copyfile(shipped, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), out))

It must actually create ./test_readme.py, because upstream's conftest calls `os.rename("test_readme.py", "tests/test_readme.py")` unconditionally and would otherwise raise FileNotFoundError.

Verified: with upstream conftest.py + this shim (/tmp/audit_spec/ws2) collection succeeds -> 10 tests collected. With the current workspace conftest.py + this shim (/tmp/audit_spec/ws4) -> 10 passed, tests/test_readme.py byte-unchanged, no stray files left at the repo root (the copy-out/replace-back round-trips to a no-op). Note the real `pytest_readme` package, if installed, still shadows this shim since site-packages resolution wins only if the root is not first — so also consider `pip install pytest-readme` in the grading image if that is under your control; the shim is the change that lives inside /workspace.

Independently reproduce the claim yourself with concrete commands (copying to /tmp scratch if you
need to mutate anything — NEVER touch /workspace). Then decide:

  * Is the problem REAL and reachable by a plausible grading run of the official test suite?
  * Or is it hypothetical / already handled / a style nit / based on a misreading?
  * Crucially: would the suggested fix RISK BREAKING the official tests by deviating from the
    upstream reference implementation at /tmp/ct_repo? Fidelity to upstream is the single most
    important property of this project, because the official tests were written against upstream.
    A "fix" that changes csv_trimming/*.py behaviour away from upstream should be refuted unless
    the finding is a genuine crash reachable from the official tests.

Default to refuted=true when uncertain. Set recommendation='fix' ONLY if you reproduced a real
problem AND the fix is safe.

"""Script to setup the test_readme.py file in the tests directory.

The `pytest_readme` package turns the python snippets contained in the
`README.md` file into an executable test module, so that the documentation
is guaranteed to stay in sync with the code. When the package is not
available, or the README cannot be converted, we silently skip the step:
a pre-generated `tests/test_readme.py` may already be shipped alongside the
test suite, and in any case a missing readme test must not break the
collection of the rest of the test suite.
"""

import os

HERE = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))
TESTS_DIRECTORY = os.path.join(HERE, "tests")
GENERATED_README_TEST = os.path.join(HERE, "test_readme.py")
TARGET_README_TEST = os.path.join(TESTS_DIRECTORY, "test_readme.py")


def _setup_readme_tests() -> None:
    """Generate the readme test module inside of the tests directory."""
    try:
        from pytest_readme import setup  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    except ImportError:
        return

    setup()

    os.makedirs(TESTS_DIRECTORY, exist_ok=True)

    if os.path.exists(GENERATED_README_TEST):
        os.replace(GENERATED_README_TEST, TARGET_README_TEST)


_setup_readme_tests()
=== UPSTREAM CONFTEST ===
"""Script to setup the test_readme.py file in the tests directory."""

import os
from pytest_readme import setup

setup()
os.rename("test_readme.py", "tests/test_readme.py")

"""Setup for the csv_trimming package."""
import os
import re
from setuptools import find_packages, setup

here = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))

# Get the long description from the relevant file
with open(os.path.join(here, 'README.md'), encoding='utf8') as f:
    long_description = f.read()


def read(*parts):
    with open(os.path.join(here, *parts), 'r', encoding='utf8') as fp:
        return fp.read()


def find_version(*file_paths):
    version_file = read(*file_paths)
    version_match = re.search(r"^__version__ = ['\"]([^'\"]*)['\"]",
                              version_file, re.M)
    if version_match:
        return version_match.group(1)
    raise RuntimeError("Unable to find version string.")

    "validate_version_code",

]

# ## Advanced trimming with row correlation
# Sometimes, the CSVs you are working with may have a row correlation, meaning part of a given row is inserted in the next row. Such cases are common when the data-entry clerk wants to make the whole table fit in their screen, and in order to do so, they split the row in two. While this is clearly an extremely bad practice, it happens in the real world and the CSV Trimmer can handle it with a little help.
# 
# You just need to provide a function that defines which rows are correlated, and the CSV Trimmer will take care of the rest. While in this example we are using a rather simple function and a relatively clean CSV, the package can handle more complex cases.
# 
def test_line_66():
    from typing import Tuple
    import pandas as pd
    from csv_trimming import CSVTrimmer
    
    def simple_correlation_callback(
        current_row: pd.Series,
        next_row: pd.Series
    ) -> Tuple[bool, pd.Series]:
        """Return the correlation between two rows.
        
        Parameters
        ----------
        current_row : pd.Series
            The current row being analyzed in the DataFrame.
        next_row : pd.Series
            The next row in the DataFrame.
    
        Returns
        -------
        Tuple[bool, pd.Series]
            A tuple with a boolean indicating if the rows are correlated
            and a Series with the merged row.
        """
    
        # All of the rows that have a subsequent correlated row are
        # non-empty, and the subsequent correlated rows are always
        # with the first cell empty.
        if pd.isna(next_row.iloc[0]) and all(pd.notna(current_row)):
            return True, pd.concat(
                [
                    current_row,
                    pd.Series({"surname": next_row.iloc[-1]}),
                ]
            )
    
        return False, current_row
    
    csv = pd.read_csv("tests/test.csv")
    trimmer = CSVTrimmer(simple_correlation_callback)
    result = trimmer.trim(csv)

"""Test suite to verify that the CLI of the package works as expected.

The CLI commands are of the form:

```bash
csv-trim input.csv output.csv
```

where `input.csv` is the path to the input CSV file and `output.csv` is the path to save the cleaned CSV file.

The CLI also supports the following options:

- `--restore-header`: Attempts to restore the header.
- `--drop-padding`: Attempts to drop padding.
- `--drop-duplicated-schema`: Attempts to drop duplicated schema.

The tests in this module verify that the CLI commands work as expected.
"""
import os
import subprocess
import pandas as pd
from csv_trimming import CSVTrimmer

def test_cli():
    """Test that the CLI works as expected."""

    paths = [
        "tests/test.csv",
        "tests/documents/noisy/padding.csv",
        "tests/documents/noisy/duplicated_schema.csv",
        "tests/documents/noisy/sicilia.csv",
    ]

    for path in paths:
        for restore_header in (True, False):
            for drop_padding in (True, False):
                for drop_duplicated_schema in (True, False):
                    trimmer = CSVTrimmer()
                    csv = pd.read_csv(path)
                    cleaned_csv = trimmer.trim(
                        csv,
                        restore_header=restore_header,
                        drop_padding=drop_padding,
                        drop_duplicated_schema=drop_duplicated_schema,
                    )

                    # We store the cleaned CSV in a temporary file
                    cleaned_csv.to_csv("tests/output.tmp.csv", index=False)

                    # We reload the cleaned CSV from the temporary file
                    cleaned_csv = pd.read_csv("tests/output.tmp.csv")

                    # We create the same output with the CLI and compare
                    # the results

                    status = subprocess.run(
                        [
                            "csv-trim",
                            path,
                            "tests/output.tmp.cli.csv",
                            *(("--no-restore-header",) if not restore_header else ()),
                            *(("--keep-padding",) if not drop_padding else ()),
                            *(("--keep-duplicated-schema",) if not drop_duplicated_schema else ()),
                        ],
                        check=True,
                    )

                    assert status.returncode == 0

                    cli_cleaned_csv = pd.read_csv("tests/output.tmp.cli.csv")

                    assert cleaned_csv.equals(cli_cleaned_csv)

                    # We remove the temporary files
                    os.remove("tests/output.tmp.cli.csv")
                    os.remove("tests/output.tmp.csv")

The mechanical claim reproduces, but the scenario is not a plausible grading run and the proposed fix is demonstrably unsafe — it creates NEW total-collection failures and silently disables a declared dependency.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (all reproduced independently)
- `pytest_readme` is genuinely absent: `python -c "import pytest_readme"` -> ModuleNotFoundError; `md.version('pytest-readme')` -> PackageNotFoundError. `pip list` shows pytest 8.4.1, pytest-cov, random-csv-generator, ugly-csv-generator, csv-trimming 1.1.1 (editable /workspace) — no pytest-readme.
- Swapping in upstream's conftest (/tmp/refute_ct/ws2) does abort collection: `ImportError while loading conftest ... ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pytest_readme'`. Same thing happens if you just run `python -m pytest` inside /tmp/ct_repo itself — i.e. UPSTREAM AS-SHIPPED does not run in this environment.
- Baseline verbatim copy (/tmp/refute_ct/ws): 10 passed. `--collect-only` lists exactly the 10 upstream tests. Package source is byte-identical to upstream.
- /workspace/conftest.py is a strict behavioral SUPERSET of upstream's: when pytest_readme IS importable it does the same two things (setup(); move ./test_readme.py -> tests/test_readme.py), and degrades to a no-op when it is not.

WHY THE SCENARIO IS NOT REACHABLE
1. /workspace/conftest.py is a ROOT-level project file, not a test file. The grading model is "the official test suite" = upstream `tests/`. tests/*.py and all 10 data files are already byte-identical to upstream, so a tests/ overlay is a no-op.
2. Decisive: /workspace/setup.py deliberately diverges from upstream with spec-MANDATED version pins (scipy>=1.10.0, random_csv_generator>=1.0.0, ugly_csv_generator>=1.1.4). If the grader restored upstream ROOT files, it would clobber those mandated pins, making the spec self-contradictory. Root files belong to the implementation, not the grader.
3. The failing combination requires an incoherent grader: it restores upstream's conftest.py (which hard-requires pytest-readme) but does NOT honor upstream's environment contract. `pytest-readme` is declared in test_deps of BOTH upstream and /workspace setup.py, and upstream CI (.github/workflows/python.yml, byte-identical in /workspace) runs `pip install ".[test]"` then `pytest`. Any grader faithful enough to restore upstream's conftest would install upstream's test extras, and the import would succeed.

WHY THE PROPOSED FIX IS UNSAFE (three concrete problems, all reproduced)
1. The finding's shadowing note is BACKWARDS, and the real direction is harmful. pytest's `prepend` import mode puts the root conftest's directory at sys.path[0], so `/workspace/pytest_readme.py` SHADOWS any installed pytest-readme. Control experiment: with a marker `pytest_readme.py` on PYTHONPATH (which outranks site-packages), the shimless copy calls it 1 time; the shimmed copy calls it 0 times. So if the grading image does `pip install .[test]`, the shim silently disables the declared dependency and test_readme.py is never regenerated from README.md.
2. The shim converts a working run into a zero. `cd tests && pytest` — baseline collects and runs 10 tests (3 pass, 7 fail on upstream's cwd-relative paths). With the shim: `shutil.SameFileError: '.../tests/test_readme.py' and '.../tests/test_readme.py' are the same file`, raised inside conftest import -> 0 tests collected. The shim writes to os.getcwd() while the conftest reads from HERE, so any cwd != rootdir is a hazard.
3. It does not even fix the claimed scenario robustly. With upstream conftest + shim but tests/test_readme.py absent (a very plausible variant — that file is a GENERATED artifact that upstream's conftest recreates on every run), collection still aborts: `FileNotFoundError: 'test_readme.py' -> 'tests/test_readme.py'` (/tmp/refute_ct/ws6). The CURRENT workspace conftest handles exactly that case gracefully via its `os.path.exists` guard.

Net: the shim only helps in the narrow intersection (upstream conftest restored AND pytest-readme absent AND tests/test_readme.py present AND cwd == rootdir), while adding a root-level module that exists nowhere upstream, is collected under `pytest.ini`'s `--doctest-modules`, hijacks a real package name, and introduces a fresh 0-test failure mode. Under the far more likely grading run (tests/ overlay, current conftest) the workspace already scores 10/10, and the current conftest is the more defensive of the two. Fidelity to upstream plus zero-downside argues for leaving /workspace untouched. If pytest-readme's absence is a real worry, the correct lever is outside the repo: `pip install pytest-readme` in the grading image.
